question: What should I check before leaving for an Erasmus exchange?
expected_key_points: Wait for the Outgoing Mobility Office email before starting the host university application.
Respect the host university application deadlines.
Complete a Learning Agreement of at least 30 ECTS and obtain the required signatures.
Complete the OLS language evaluation if the teaching language is not the student's mother tongue.
Complete the required enrolment steps and upload the signed mobility contract through the mobility portal.
Arrange accommodation and check health insurance, passport validity and visa requirements.
answer:
Before leaving for an Erasmus exchange, you should check and complete several administrative, health, and travel requirements:

- Check that your European health insurance card is valid for the whole mobility period, and download the International SOS assistance app, following the instructions received via email (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). Note that International SOS provides 24/7 assistance for mobility trips but is not an insurance provider (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Luxembourgish students should report their trip to the MAEE for safety reasons (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Check passport validity and visa requirements, as some partner institutions require validity beyond your mobility period (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Arrange your accommodation early, as rooms are limited, and beware of housing scams (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Ensure you have signed your mobility contract (grant agreement) before departure or during the first month of mobility, and ensure that your bank details on the contract match the information on your Guichet Etudiant (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Check that you have completed your mandatory learning agreement (LA or OLA) covering at least 30 ECTS, which must be signed by you, your programme director (via your faculty's mobility contact), and your host institution (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Take the Erasmus+ language evaluation if the teaching language is not your mother tongue (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

If you need clarification regarding Erasmus+ or student mobility, it is recommended that you contact the International Relations Office (BRI), which is responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

question: Which documents should I prepare for Erasmus registration?
expected_key_points: Prepare a Learning Agreement (LA or OLA) covering at least 30 ECTS.
Obtain the required signatures from the student, programme director and host institution.
Upload the signed mobility contract through the mobility portal.
Complete the OLS language evaluation if the teaching language is not the student's mother tongue.
answer:
To prepare for your Erasmus mobility, several compulsory documents and administrative items are required depending on your specific situation:

- Erasmus+ Mobility Contract (Grant Agreement): A compulsory administrative document containing details about your semester of mobility, grant amount (if eligible), and obligations, which must be signed by you and the Vice-Rector https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Learning Agreement (LA) or Online Learning Agreement (OLA): A document outlining your course selections (totaling 30 ECTS for Bachelor students) https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573 (Last checked: 14.11.2026). If the host university does not use the online form, you complete the Word version of the Learning Agreement and have it validated by your faculty contact https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Supporting documents for the "Fewer Opportunities" top-up (if applicable): Depending on your case, this may include a doctor-completed and signed form confirming a disability or severe/chronic illness, a household composition certificate and proof that children spent the mobility period abroad, or a residence permit indicating refugee status https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Health and Safety Items: A valid European Health Insurance Card, downloading the International SOS assistance app, and reporting your trip to the MAEE if you are a Luxembourgish student https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).
- Certificates and Post-Arrival Documents: Certificates of arrival and end of stay (departure), the online mobility report, and your original Transcript of Records from the host university which must be provided to your academic contact upon return https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

Missing Information:
The provided sources do not specify every exact personal application form that may be required by individual partner receiving institutions during their specific application processes (Step 3 on the landing page) https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

Recommendation:
If you need clarification or guidance regarding Erasmus+ and student mobility, it is recommended to contact the International Relations Office (BRI) / Outgoing Mobility Office at bri.outgoing@uni.lu, as they are responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf (Last checked: 12.11.2026), https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/ (Last checked: 12.11.2026).

question: How can I check whether my courses will transfer as credits?
expected_key_points: Agree on the courses and their recognition through the Learning Agreement.
Use the Learning Agreement to record the courses and ECTS.
If courses change during mobility, update the Learning Agreement using Table A2.
Provide reasons for exceptional course changes.
Obtain the required signatures from the student, host institution and sending institution.
Credits agreed in the Learning Agreement and confirmed by the Transcript of Records are automatically recognised according to the form.
answer:
To check whether your courses will transfer as credits, you must ensure they are included in your Learning Agreement (or Online Learning Agreement) and approved beforehand by both your home study programme and your host institution (https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). By signing the Learning Agreement, the home university agrees to validate your courses upon your return if they are successfully completed (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/02/FDEF-How-to-create-and-fill-out-my-Online-Learning-Agreement-OLA-FDEF.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

According to definitions on the Learning Agreement changes form, automatic recognition applies to all credits gained abroad as agreed in the Learning Agreement and confirmed by the Transcript of Records, meaning they will be transferred without delay and counted toward your degree without additional work or assessment (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/Modification_Learning_Agreement_Erasmus_outgoing_students.docx, Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

After your mobility, the recognition of ECTS requires the host university to issue a Transcript of Records, and only credits from courses approved on your final Learning Agreement will be validated (https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/free-mover/, Last checked: 14.11.2026). You are responsible for obtaining this transcript and having the host university send a copy directly to your faculty contact (such as Stephanie Anderson for FDEF) (https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/02/Checklist-Free-mover_SEMP_EN.pdf, Last checked: 14.11.2026).

If you are seeking clarification about Erasmus+ or student mobility, I recommend contacting the International Relations Office (BRI / BRIO), as it is responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility.

question: How should I plan health insurance for studying abroad in Europe?
expected_key_points: Arrange adequate health insurance before travelling.
Know that International SOS provides free 24/7 assistance for mobility trips.
Understand that International SOS is not an insurance provider and does not replace health insurance.
answer:
For studying abroad in Europe, you should check that your European health insurance card (CNS) is valid for the whole duration of your stay abroad (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/02/Checklist-Free-mover_SEMP_EN.pdf, Last checked: 14.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). Additionally, you should get adequate health insurance and download the International SOS assistance app, following the instructions sent by email (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). Please note that the International SOS app provides free 24/7 assistance for mobility trips, but it is not an insurance provider (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

If you have questions or need clarification about Erasmus+ or student mobility, it is recommended that you contact the International Relations Office (BRI), as it is responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility.

question: What questions should I ask about accommodation before travelling?
expected_key_points: Consider accommodation costs when comparing the cost of living at the destination.
Check the location of the host university campus because courses may take place away from the main study location.
Consider accommodation availability and location when preparing for the exchange.
Understand that accommodation is the student's responsibility and that applying early is recommended.
answer:
Based on the official sources, the specific questions you should ask about accommodation before travelling are not detailed. However, the sources note that accommodation is your responsibility and warn that rooms are limited and that you should beware of housing scams (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026). When choosing a receiving institution, you should also check living costs, which include accommodation (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026). 

The official sources do not cover a specific checklist of questions to ask regarding accommodation. 

Recommendation: As the sources state that finding accommodation is your responsibility, you may wish to ask your host institution about application deadlines for student housing, the availability of rooms on or near campus, estimated monthly rent costs, and whether they provide official housing assistance or verified lists of local rentals to help you avoid scams. If you need further guidance or clarification about your student mobility, it is recommended to contact the International Relations Office (BRI), as it is responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/erasmus-before-study-exchange/, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

question: How can I make an exchange budget that includes hidden costs?
expected_key_points: Estimate living expenses such as accommodation, food and leisure.
Consider differences in the cost of living between destinations.
Check the Erasmus monthly grant applicable to the destination.
Consider the travel contribution, which depends on the distance band.
Check whether eligible students can receive the fewer-opportunities top-up.
Account for the minimum and maximum funded mobility durations.
Plan for upfront expenses because 70% of the grant is paid at the beginning and the remaining amount is recalculated after mobility.
answer:
I couldn't find information about hidden costs or how to build an exchange budget that includes them in the official information available to me. 

However, the official sources do provide details on available financial support and grants for student mobility, such as monthly contributions to living costs categorized by country groups, travel cost allowances based on distance, and a fewer opportunities top-up (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/depliant_YourExchangeSemester.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

If you have questions about Erasmus+ or student mobility, it is recommended to contact the International Relations Office (BRI), which is responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility (https://www.uni.lu/en/about/organisation/administration/international-relations-office/, Last checked: 12.11.2026). You can reach the Outgoing Mobility Office (BRI) at bri.outgoing@uni.lu (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/07/08160616/Financement_Financial_-Erasmus_25-26_FR-EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). Please consult the University's Erasmus+ guidance or contact the relevant mobility office for further assistance.

question: Which deadlines should I put in an Erasmus preparation checklist?
expected_key_points: Regularly check the university student email account for mobility instructions.
Ensure the European Health Insurance Card is valid before departure.
After arrival, obtain the signed and stamped Certificate of Arrival and upload it to the mobility portal.
Update the Learning Agreement within the first month after arrival if courses or ECTS change.
At the end of the exchange, obtain and upload the Certificate of End of Stay and the required Learning Agreement documents.
Complete the online mobility report.
After returning, provide the required Transcript of Records to the academic contact.
answer:
Based on the official sources, there are no specific calendar dates published for an Erasmus preparation checklist, as deadlines are generally not published on the landing pages and specific application or submission deadlines are not listed (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

However, the sources provide relative timing and recurring schedules that you can include in your preparation checklist:

- General preparation: You should prepare for your mobility semester one academic year before departure (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- Mandatory info session: Attend the Study Abroad Day information session, which takes place annually in November on the second Thursday (https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026).
- Mobility contract: The mobility contract must be signed before your departure or during the first month of your mobility (https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2024/10/FAQ-Erasmus-FR_DE_-EN_24-25.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

What is missing: The official sources do not provide exact calendar deadlines for applications, course registrations, or final document submissions (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/, Last checked: 12.11.2026). 

Recommendation: Since the International Relations Office (BRI) is responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility, you should seek clarification and specific calendar deadlines by contacting the BRI at bri.outgoing@uni.lu (https://www.uni.lu/en/mobility/outgoing-student-mobility/erasmus/, Last checked: 12.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=10573, Last checked: 14.11.2026; https://www.uni.lu/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2025/05/Checklist-Erasmus_EN.pdf, Last checked: 12.11.2026).

question: When should I contact my home university coordinator during an exchange?
expected_key_points: Recognise that the programme director is responsible for recognising ECTS earned abroad.
Understand that credit recognition is based on the Learning Agreement signed before the exchange.
Recommend contacting the programme director or relevant faculty mobility contact about academic recognition or agreed courses, while identifying this as a recommendation.
answer:
Based on the official sources, during your exchange stay you should stay in touch with your faculty mobility contact person, your programme director, and the Outgoing Mobility Office (Last checked: 14.11.2026, https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305). Specifically, you should contact them or modify your Learning Agreement if some of the courses you chose do not run after you arrive (Last checked: 14.11.2026, https://www.uni.lu/en/?p=12305).

Regarding advice or a recommended next step, if you have any questions or need clarification about Erasmus+ or student mobility, it is recommended that you contact the International Relations Office (BRI), as it is responsible for coordinating Erasmus+ student mobility (Last checked: 12.11.2026, https://www.uni.lu/fdef-en/study-abroad/).
